# Final project quality report — SmartGrid AI

*Generated by `python -m src.final.report` from the result files; every number is traceable to `reports/final/*.json`, `reports/phase2/*` or `experiments/*`.*

## 1. What was audited
All Python packages, the FastAPI backend, the React frontend, configuration, simulator, evaluation, calibration, confidence, explainability, streaming, incident replay, ONNX, tests, dependencies, experiment artefacts, README and UI text. Findings are listed in [`final_project_audit.md`](final_project_audit.md).

## 2. What was fixed
- **Security:** path traversal in the SPA fallback (confirmed exploitable, fixed, regression-tested); unvalidated request bodies (now Pydantic schemas with bounds); stack-trace leakage (global handler); CORS narrowed.
- **Bugs:** order-dependent backend tests, a production route clash, stale-cache display, a meaningless 'sensor noise' criterion (43 % base rate → 2.8 %), and a '100 %' risk display.
- **Methodology:** single-realisation validation replaced by a 3-seed × 5-simulation protocol; thresholds and calibration re-derived on fresh validation; a test proves decisions ignore test data.
- **Code quality:** 91 lint findings → 0; duplicated inference unified; exact dependency pins.
- **Final polish pass:** one source of truth for thresholds (`deployment.json`, used by API and CLI — the CLI tools previously still used the Phase-1 threshold), confidence bins and model window/horizon labels (served by the API, no UI hard-coding); Incident Replay and the incident list showed a stale Phase-1 'offline lead time' (now the final evaluation; equals the engine for all 40 test failures, tested); Model Lab presented the deployed model with Phase-1 metrics (now labelled, with a separate deployed-OP row); `/api/system` latency now from the final benchmark; an `eval()` replaced by `ast.literal_eval`; Windows-invalid checkpoint file names; a test that was skipped on fresh clones (needed a local frontend build) now runs everywhere; dataset-licence clean-up (§20).

## 3. What was improved
- Formal temporal-integrity suite (16 tests), API robustness suite, frontend unit tests.
- `/api/ready`, `/api/model`, `/api/metrics`, `/api/predict`; request IDs; structured logs; startup model loading.
- Streaming engine latency: feature computation via a NumPy newest-row path (7.18 → 0.51 ms p50) with identical alarm statuses.
- Simulator config file with documented mechanisms, realism knobs and 4 stress profiles; formal robustness curve.
- Refined false-alarm taxonomy with base rates, and a UI false-alarm explorer.
- Historical-pattern explanations; confidence-bin reliability; Docker and `.env.example`.

## 4. What did not improve (negative results kept)
- No alternative architecture beat GRU + attention under the protocol (table in §6).
- Training on MODERATE-varied signatures: NORMAL PR-AUC change -0.089, mean stressed gain -0.000 → not adopted.
- Robust/adaptive feature normalisations and calendar removal did not improve fresh validation.
- Cross-asset transfer remains weak (§11). int8 quantisation is smaller but slower on ARM.

## 5. Final model
GRU (64) + additive temporal attention, 65 causal stationary features, 12 h window, 2 h horizon, 31,425 parameters, served with ONNX Runtime, isotonic calibration, 3-seed confidence, integrated-gradients attribution. Weights are unchanged since Phase 1; the operating point and calibrator were re-derived under the final protocol.

## 6. Final validated metrics (held-out test, final operating point)
| Metric | Final operating point (current) | Phase-1 operating point (historical) |
|---|---|---|
| warning threshold (raw score) | 0.241 | 0.659 |
| PR-AUC / ROC-AUC | 0.326 / 0.845 | same (threshold-free) |
| precision / recall / F1 | 0.171 / 0.575 / 0.264 | 0.318 / 0.487 / 0.385 |
| failures warned: all / predictable | 62.5% / 75.8% | 60.0% / 72.7% |
| median lead time | 180 min | 120 min |
| false alarms / transformer-day | 0.250 | 0.115 |

Expected PR-AUC on fresh event realisations: **0.360 ± 0.056** [0.257, 0.475] (3 seeds × 5 simulations).

## 7. Fresh-validation methodology
See [`model_selection_protocol.md`](model_selection_protocol.md): every decision uses 3 seeds × 5 freshly re-simulated validation periods; the challenger must beat the incumbent by > max(0.01, 1 SE); thresholds and calibration come from pooled fresh validation; test is reporting-only (enforced by tests).

| Candidate | PR-AUC mean ± std [min, max] | Δ vs incumbent | replaces | params | p50 / p99 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GRU + attention (incumbent) | 0.360 ± 0.056 [0.26, 0.47] | +0.000 | no | 31,425 | 0.42 / 0.46 |
| GRU | 0.347 ± 0.044 [0.27, 0.43] | -0.013 | no | 27,265 | 0.37 / 0.40 |
| Compact GRU (h=32) | 0.342 ± 0.038 [0.28, 0.41] | -0.017 | no | 9,537 | 0.33 / 0.37 |

| Lightweight transformer | 0.283 ± 0.048 [0.19, 0.36] | -0.077 | no | 23,489 | 0.26 / 0.28 |

## 8. Calibration
Isotonic, fitted on pooled fresh validation. Test Brier 0.0248 → 0.0125; ECE 0.0390 → 0.0027. Raw score and calibrated risk are shown separately in the UI.

## 9. Confidence
| Bin | alarm-steps (original test) | precision |
|---|---|---|
| HIGH | 143 | 63% |
| MEDIUM | 236 | 13% |
| LOW | 697 | 9% |

HIGH-confidence alarms are much more often right; MEDIUM and LOW are not distinguishable. Model confidence ≠ physical certainty.

## 10. Detectability
Test failures: 40 (33 predictable, 7 sudden). Recall all 62.5%, predictable 75.8%, strong-signal 77.4%; by class {'A': '17/22', 'B': '7/9', 'C': '1/2', 'D': '0/7'}.

## 11. Generalization
**Domain-invariant feature selection** (`src/final/cross_asset.py`, PR-AUC on the target transformer's test period, 3 seeds):

| Train → test | stationary (65 features) | domain-invariant subset | in-domain (both), stationary | in-domain (both), invariant |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 → T2 | 0.133 ± 0.014 | 0.096 ± 0.018 | 0.327 | 0.298 |
| T2 → T1 | 0.242 ± 0.059 | 0.268 ± 0.036 | 0.336 | 0.317 |

Keeping only the 27 features whose distribution is similar across the two transformers (cross-asset PSI < 0.1 on unlabelled training data) changed cross-asset PR-AUC by -0.005 on average (3 seeds per direction): no meaningful improvement, so it is **not adopted** (negative result).

## 12. Robustness
Deployed configuration, test period, 5 re-simulations × 3 seeds per level (see README table and `reports/final/robustness_curve.png`).

## 13. False alarms
52 episodes (0.250/transformer-day): harmless simulated disturbance 24, sensor noise 1, seasonal / slow thermal behaviour 1, unusual real sensor behaviour 15, model error 11, unknown / simulation artefact 0. Details and base rates: [`final_false_alarm_analysis.md`](final_false_alarm_analysis.md).

## 14. Lead time
Median 180 min, mean 211 min, range 15–690 min (engine-measured; equals the offline evaluation, tested).

## 15. Performance
Apple M2, 1 thread, idle machine: engine step p50/p95/p99 5.49 / 5.68 / 6.07 ms; ONNX inference p50 0.072 ms vs PyTorch 0.391 ms; NumPy newest-row features 0.51 ms. Full tables: [`performance_benchmark.md`](performance_benchmark.md).

## 16. Frontend architecture
React 19 + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind + Framer Motion + Recharts + Zustand. A shared clock store (`src/store/grid.ts`) syncs every view: engine-log mode for scrubbing, live mode for real engine sessions. 7 routes. Status uses icon + text + colour; keyboard and reduced-motion support; `cache: no-store`; client perf trace.

## 17. Backend architecture
FastAPI with lifespan model loading, an intelligence engine (features → ONNX → calibration → confidence → attribution → risk → alerts), a session manager, Pydantic schemas, structured logs with request IDs, a metrics endpoint, and path-safe static serving.

## 18. Test results
**Python:** `pytest` 85 passed, 0 skipped (unit, integration, API robustness, 16 temporal-integrity, streaming). The one test previously skipped on fresh clones (`test_spa_shell_is_not_cached`, needed a local frontend build) now uses a temporary build directory and runs everywhere. `ruff`: all checks passed. `pip-audit`: no known vulnerabilities. **Clean-copy reproduction** (only files git would commit): `make setup` → `make data` → `make check` all exit 0.

**Frontend:** `tsc` 0 errors; `oxlint` 0 warnings; Vitest 13 passed; production build OK; `npm audit`: 0 vulnerabilities. **Browser:** all 7 routes load with 0 console errors and 0 failed requests; Incident Replay (T2 thermal runaway) shows FIRST RELIABLE WARNING 3h 00m BEFORE FAILURE, equal to the offline evaluation; Demo Mode streams the real engine on held-out data; backend-down state shows a clear banner (dev server).

## 19. Security review
Path traversal fixed; validated inputs with bounds; narrowed CORS; no secrets in the repo (`.env.example` only); no subprocess calls in the API; no `eval`/`exec`; pickle loaded only for the project's own locally produced preprocessor; `pip-audit` and `npm audit`: 0 known vulnerabilities; no debug mode; FastAPI docs remain enabled (demo). No authentication (local single-user demo; stated, not hidden).

## 20. Reproducibility review
Exact pinned requirements; seeded simulator (bit-for-bit test); seeds for all training; trained weights are not published (unresolved CC BY-ND status) and are retrained by `make data` — bit-identical on the dev machine. ETDataset is CC BY-ND 4.0, so files with row-level (adapted) sensor values — processed data, the engine log, stream CSVs — are git-ignored and rebuilt deterministically by `make data` (see `DATASET.md`). Verified from a clean copy of only the files git would commit: `make setup` → `make data` → full test suite. Three-command quick start in the README. Dockerfile and compose provided (**not built: Docker unavailable on the development machine**).

## 21. Remaining limitations
Simulated labels (accelerated failure rate); two assets; weak cross-asset transfer; 40 test failures; seed variance; no voltage/current/frequency/weather; low precision at the chosen operating point; idealised simulator despite stress profiles; Docker untested here.

## 22. Recommended future research
Real trip and maintenance labels with rolling-origin evaluation over many assets; additional channels (DGA, winding temperature, voltage, current, ambient); hierarchical or fine-tuned models for transfer; cost-based thresholds with operators; a validated rule + model hybrid; conformal risk intervals.

## Resume Project Readiness

No scores — strengths and remaining limitations per dimension.

| Dimension | Strengths | Remaining limitations |
|---|---|---|
| Technical maturity | End-to-end system: data → simulation → features → model → calibration → streaming engine → API → UI, all wired to one deployment manifest. | Research prototype; single process; no auth, persistence beyond JSON acks, or deployment pipeline. |
| ML methodology | Leakage-safe splits with embargo; causal features; 3-seed × 5-simulation selection with a pre-declared margin; validation-only thresholds/calibration; negative results kept. | Labels are simulated; 40 test failures → wide uncertainty; idealised simulator despite stress profiles. |
| Reproducibility | Pinned deps, seeded simulator (bit-for-bit test), `make setup / data / demo / check`, verified from a clean copy. | First `make data` retrains the deployed models (~20–30 min); full research pipeline ~2.5 h; Docker image never built; tested on macOS (arm64) only. |
| Security | Path traversal found and fixed with regression test; Pydantic validation; no stack traces; narrowed CORS; 0 known dependency vulnerabilities. | No authentication or rate limiting (local demo). |
| Performance | Engine step ≈ 5.5 ms p50 (14.3 → 5.5 ms via NumPy newest-row features); ONNX 5.4× faster than eager PyTorch; p50/p95/p99 reported. | Measured on one laptop; attribution + confidence dominate the step. |
| Frontend quality | 7 data-driven routes, Incident Replay, guided Demo Mode on real held-out data, responsive, reduced-motion, backend-down state. | Desktop-first; frontend perf trace measured once (earlier session). |
| Testing | 85 Python tests (16 temporal-integrity), 13 Vitest tests, 0 skipped; lint, types, build, audits in `make check`. | No browser end-to-end test suite (UI verified manually + scripted screenshots). |
| Research credibility | Every metric traceable to `reports/final/*.json`; recall over all vs predictable failures; false-alarm base rates; historical vs final clearly separated. | Not validated on real failures or other transformers. |

**Recommended resume claims** (defensible): leakage-safe temporal evaluation; GRU + temporal attention selected under a
3-seed × 5-simulation protocol; held-out PR-AUC 0.326 / ROC-AUC 0.845; 75.8 % of predictable *simulated* failures
warned, median 3 h ahead, at 0.25 false alarms per transformer-day; isotonic calibration (Brier 0.025 → 0.013);
5.5 ms p50 streaming step, ONNX 0.07 ms; FastAPI + React/TypeScript; path-traversal fix; automated temporal-integrity tests.

**Claims that must NOT be made:** real-world deployment or utility use; blackout or outage prevention; prediction of
real/unseen physical failures; "X % accuracy"; causal explanations; state-of-the-art; certified or production-grade;
cross-transformer generalisation; Docker image tested.

Full checklist: [`final_resume_readiness.md`](final_resume_readiness.md).
